suggestions.title: “I see you. I'm not going to force my way past you.”

edits.before: Talk to the guard the way your Nurturer talks to your inner child: “I see you. I'm not going to force my way past you. What's going on?” Then wait and listen patiently. If nothing comes back, that's okay, you don't need to push for an answer. Later on, you can ask it, “What are you afraid would happen if you stopped protecting me by…?”
edits.after: You can tell that part something like, “I see you. I'm not going to force my way past you. What's going on?” Or however you'd actually say that. Then wait and listen patiently. If nothing comes, that's fine for now. No need to answer for that part just because you'd set this up as a healing session. Later on, you can ask it, “What are you afraid would happen if you stopped protecting me by…?”

suggestions.title: “… that one can sting …”

edits.before: You could say something like 'What are you protecting me from?' or 'Are you afraid I will lie to myself again?' or 'Are you afraid this will just be a performance?' If it says yes, that can sting, because there could be something to it. Maybe you've fooled yourself before, and that part of you remembers it. "Tell me what you remember, I'm listening." works well here.
edits.after: You could say something like 'What are you protecting me from?' or 'Are you afraid I will lie to myself again?' or 'Are you afraid this will just be a performance?' If it says yes, that one can sting, because there could be something to it. Maybe you've fooled yourself before, and that part remembers. "Tell me what you remember, I'm listening." works well here. It puts you into the role of the Nurturer, which alleviates the instinct to argue back.

suggestions.what: Your inner child guide’s lines go back as you wrote them (“that one can sting”, “that part remembers”), with your sentence that says why the question works: “It puts you into the role of the Nurturer, which alleviates the instinct to argue back.”
